year.label: 2016 Cayman GT4 Clubsport with the Manthey MR kit

identity.real_world_identity_notes: Customer racing Cayman GT4 Clubsport of the 981 generation, with the Manthey Racing MR kit. Curated first as the 2019 718 Clubsport of the 982 generation, which was wrong: the Extended Car Info spreadsheet this record was imported from carried the wrong year, and its author has since corrected it, noting that AMS2's interior matches the previous version. The simulator said so all along - AMS2 names the car "Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR" without the "718" that marks the 982. The error surfaced when Assetto Corsa EVO's 718 Clubsport turned out to model a different steering wheel and dash; that is a different real car and wants its own record rather than a second entry here.

wheel_rim.notes: Re-observed in the AMS2 cockpit as a conventional rim flattened at the bottom, which is d-shaped in this project's vocabulary; it was first recorded as round. It is a conventional rim rather than a control-panel one, and flattening alone never makes a rim gt-formula. This describes the 981 cockpit AMS2 models. No reviewed source establishes the real car's rim.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.

AMS2 1.6.9.91 nonetheless required clutch input to move off. That is recorded as an explicit simulator override, so the in-sim guidance tells the driver to use the clutch while the record keeps the real car's value.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip.

AMS2 models the 2016 Clubsport of the 981 generation. The record first described the 2019 718 of the 982 generation, and the gearbox construction and standing-start clutch were inherited from that car's manufacturer material. Both are now unknown and need sources for the 981.

AMS2 requires clutch input to move off, which the guided drive established and an override records. Whether the real car has a clutch pedal at all depends on its gearbox, which is no longer established, so the override no longer claims to be a deviation from a known real-car value.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.porsche-cayman-gt4-clubsport-mr.20260813t171028562z-e4f6b4a0 by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: AMS2 1.6.9.91 requires clutch input to move off. Recorded so the driver is told to use the clutch in this simulator while the real car's requirement stays unknown; it previously read as a deviation from a clutch-pedal-free PDK, which was the 982's specification rather than this car's.

confidence.basis: Directly observed in the guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is established by a registered manufacturer source.

claims.basis: The spreadsheet author's own correction establishes that AMS2 models the 2016 Clubsport of the 981 generation, and the exact simulator identity was observed live. Short of verified because the correction is a forum post rather than manufacturer material, and no 981 source has been reviewed for this record yet. Falsified by Reiza or Coanda stating a different model year, or by 981 material that does not match the modelled car.

Six paddle-selected gears on a sequential gate were counted directly in the guided drive. Porsche's and Manthey's material previously supported this and has been removed: both describe the 982, which is not the car AMS2 models. The gearbox construction rested on them alone and is now unknown; the gear count and actuation did not, because the drive saw them.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive established that AMS2 requires clutch input to move off, which differs from the real car's clutch-pedal-free PDK.

Both were inherited from the wrong generation. Porsche's 718 launch material specifies a six-speed dual-clutch PDK for the 982, and the record reasoned from it that a PDK has no clutch pedal so a standing start needs none. Neither reaches the 981 this simulator models, and neither is observable in a drive: a guided drive sees how a driver asks for a gear, not how the gearbox is built, and AMS2's demand for clutch input is what the simulator does rather than what the car requires. Established by material for the 2016 Clubsport - the Manthey technical manual of that year is the likeliest source.

archetype.basis:
Five archetypes survive the gaps, and that is the cost of the correction made visible. The record used to deviate from one mechanism because Porsche's 718 material named a dual-clutch PDK and the reasoning that a PDK has no clutch pedal settled the standing start. That material describes the 982; AMS2 models the 2016 Clubsport of the 981 generation, so both values came out and three fields are now open together: gearbox_type, standing_start_clutch and throttle_lift.

What survives is every six-speed paddle mechanism with an automatic cut and blip - sequential, semi-automatic and dog box, each with and without a clutch from rest. One source for the 981's gearbox would close most of them at once, because the construction and the clutch pedal travel together on a car of this kind.
